statement: The maximum number of real smooth plane quartics through twelve general real points and tangent to two general real lines is 36.

answer.text: With two line tangencies, the maximum is 36 and total reality is attained.

source.location: Theorem 1 and Section 2.2, specialized to degree 4 and two line tangencies (printed pp.2,5–6)

scope: Smooth irreducible degree-4 plane curves through twelve general real points and tangent to two general real lines.
notes:
Here k denotes the number of tangent-line conditions. Other k are not settled by these cited statements.

Felice Ronga, A real Riemann-Hurwitz theorem (2000, article ID ronga_2000_real_riemann_hurwitz). The one-tangency statement is represented by its own result record.

This is the two-tangency specialization of Bertrand’s total-reality theorem.
